_comment: Brushed stainless steel: the satin, belt-grained finish of appliance fronts, range hoods and sinks. Opaque, a conductor, with specular anisotropy: the grooves (the article's own normal and roughness, L2, gen_stainlesssteel_brushed.py) run along V, so the highlight stretches along U, as on Aluminium_Brushed. Colour is the Physically Based constant, as on StainlessSteel_Polished. APPROXIMATE: no metal edge tint (F82 specular_color) or complex IOR (F-LC-6). Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): hairline scratches (overlay 1, damage), dust as a deposit (Phase10), fingerprints, gated by the Edges mask (B the corner band for a deposit, A the open faces for handling marks, so dust takes slot 2 and fingerprints slot 3). Drafted by /matter-generate for the Kitchen_set look; Storm only, not rigged.
name: StainlessSteel_Brushed_Clean_Base_s001_v01

sources.why: Physically Based gives roughness 0 (a mirror). Roughness ~0.30 in the map (0.25-0.35): a satin brushed finish. Anisotropy 0.8: long, continuous parallel grooves (no measured value; Satin's floats are 0.7).
